name: Is it better to add square footage or redesign the kitchen I already have?

mainEntity.name: Is it better to add square footage or redesign the kitchen I already have?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Adding square footage may provide more storage, work surface, and seating, but it also adds construction cost, approvals, exterior work, and potential disruption. Reworking the existing footprint can deliver better function with fewer building-envelope changes.

**Context:** A small addition may still involve foundation, roof, exterior finishes, windows, insulation, and utility extensions. An interior redesign may be more efficient when the main problem is poor circulation rather than insufficient floor area.

**Key factors:**
- Whether the kitchen lacks area or has inefficient zoning
- Cost of foundation and exterior connections
- Desired island, pantry, or dining capacity
- Property constraints and existing setbacks

**Practical guidance:** Compare two concepts: an optimized existing footprint and an expanded footprint. Measure the clearance needed around islands, appliance doors, walkways, and dining areas before committing to added area.

Elite Remodeling & Design can develop layout options around the way the household uses the home.
acceptedAnswer.description: Redesigning may solve circulation and storage problems with less exterior work, while an addition creates more room but can require structural, foundation, roof, and approval work. Compare both layouts using appliance clearances, pantry needs, island size, and the project’s total scope.
